citation.title: DQN-Based Pre-Optimization for Dual-Scale Collaborative Topology Optimization of Anisotropic Materials
citation.authors: Shuo Feng; Yuhao Yang; Ke Li; Qidong Han; Jinchen Cao; Junyi Du

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: For the MBB beam, DQN pre-optimization followed by BESO lowers reported structural compliance by 22.463% relative to the no-pre-optimization case.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: No classical-to-ML time ratio is reported; the abstract comparison concerns compliance.
claim.alternatives: The abstract also qualitatively claims faster convergence and better thermal management; conclusion describes convergence efficiency advantages.

baseline.classical_method: BESO without DQN pre-optimization (fixed penalty settings); SIMP/BESO discussed as traditional methods
baseline.implementation: BESO in numerical-analysis environment; exact implementation not stated
baseline.problem_size: Main MBB case: macro 150×80 elements and micro 50×50 elements (Table 4); separate generalization MBB 300×100 and cantilever 150×100 (Section 5.4)
baseline.classical_iterations: No-DQN comparator stopping rule/count not stated; DQN runs 60–180 iterations (Table 3)
baseline.training_time: not stated; DQN training concurrent with topology optimization (Section 3.4)
baseline.quality_metric: mechanical compliance; thermal compliance also reported
baseline.quality_gap: MBB: 0.7421 without pre-optimization vs 0.5754 with it, 22.463% reduction (Section 5.1)

R1.evidence: Abstract and Section 5.1: same MBB optimization comparison reports compliance and the reduction; Table 4 gives common macro/micro volume constraints.

R2.evidence: Sections 3.3 and 5.1 describe cross-platform implementation and a no-DQN BESO comparison, but provide no solver, hardware comparison, or per-iteration classical timing.

R3.evidence: Sections 3.4 and 5.1 make training/convergence-efficiency claims, but no training duration, data-generation cost, or break-even accounting is reported.

R4.evidence: Sections 4.2 and 5.1 report finite-element-based compliance; Table 4 specifies volume constraints, but failure or infeasibility rates are not reported.

reporting.n_test_cases: Two named geometry cases (MBB and cantilever); eight independent MBB training runs; weighting and microstructure variants (Sections 3.4, 5.2–5.5)

notes: Article states CC BY license and includes software contribution, but no public code repository is identified; retrievable article text alone does not establish runnable public code.
